  For psychometricians at testing organizations and credentialing bodies:
  Run a program from blueprint to bank monitoring, with every decision

---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Operational work needs decisions you can defend and reports that
non-statisticians can read. mirtverse wraps mirt's estimation in a documented
workflow: Each step checks the results and raises flags that a person
reviews before the next step.

## Your path in three steps

**1. Walk through the assessment pipeline.** `mv_pipeline()` takes a test
through 13 stages, from the blueprint to bank monitoring. The
[pipeline article](assessment-pipeline.html) runs a full example:

```r
library(mirtverse)
# certexam is a built-in certification exam with a scoring key
p <- mv_pipeline("Certification exam, form A")
p <- add_responses(p, certexam, items = 3:34, key = certexam_key)
p <- calibrate(p)          # fits the model and flags miskeys, misfit and DIF
flags(p)                   # what needs a decision before you move on
```

**2. Check fairness and precision.** DIF in one call, item health cards for
review meetings, and information and conditional precision at the cut score:

```r
mod <- p$model             # an ordinary mirt model
item_card(mod, "Q14")      # one-page review of a flagged item
res <- dif(scored, group = gender)   # your scored 0/1 data and a grouping variable
gg_dif(res)
```

**3. Report to people who do not use R.** A technical report from the
pipeline, a static HTML report, or an
[interactive dashboard](dashboards.html) that runs in any browser:

```r
pipeline_report(p, file = "technical-report.html")
export_dashboard(mod, "results.html", format = "html")
```

[Open the live example dashboard](../dashboard/sat12-demo.html) to see what
your stakeholders would get.

## Why you can trust the numbers

- mirtverse never changes how models are estimated; every result comes from
  mirt, and every function accepts an ordinary `mirt()` model.
- The package has an automated test suite and passes `R CMD check` on every
  change ([check status](https://github.com/okanbulut/mirtverse/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)).
- Every flag rule is listed by `mv_rules()` and can be changed, and every
  decision you acknowledge is recorded in the report.
- The workbench and `mv_ask()` show the R code they run, so analyses can be
  reviewed and rerun.
